name: Worm
overview: Scripture uses the image of a worm to convey human frailty and humility, as seen in Job's rhetorical question comparing man to a worm and in God's reassurance to 'worm Jacob' in Isaiah 41:14. Worms also symbolize decay and divine judgment, illustrated by the spoiled manna in Exodus 16 and the undying worm and unquenched fire in Isaiah 66:24 that signify eternal punishment. Additionally, the worm serves as an instrument of God's sovereign will, such as when it withered Jonah's gourd, and historically, according to Josephus, Herod Agrippa I was consumed by worms, underscoring the physical reality of divine judgment.
